title: Wire the classifier into run-epic with a credential the operator chooses
description: Triaged 2026-09-23 from wne's close-out (operator's choice A: absorb into wne). The classifier is built and never runs: run-epic constructs no jev.Client because nothing says where its credential comes from (c6f918cc). Decide the source (the gateway route with the run token in the cloud; the operator's Cloudflare credential locally), wire it, and keep the documented fallback: no credential or an unreachable classifier degrades to [tier_policy.start].
notes: 2026-09-23 15:16 - ticfac run epic-wne: attempt 10 reported a finding drafted for triage — contract "The credential-ownership bundle closes ~/.ticfacrc, so the operator cannot choose it as the local home for the classifier key" (key 8e6b611bf07bc311ffeea26dac08573fa6186b8597830600dac65e819276de5e, severity low, for this repository). Triage with `ticfac finding wne 8e6b611bf07bc311ffeea26dac08573fa6186b8597830600dac65e819276de5e --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"`, `--discard --by "<who>"`, or — when it was repaired inside this epic — `--fixed-as <commit> --by "<who>"`; the tick closes and the finding rides to the close-out, which does not hand over while it is untriaged.
acceptance_criteria: With [tier_policy] dear_work_types configured, a local run and a cloud run each classify a role-less tick through Jev and record the decision; with no credential the run falls back to [tier_policy.start] and says so; and the full suites pass
